headline: The measure would have funded federal agencies through February 8, 2019, added border and disaster money, and extended several Medicaid and other programs, but the Senate did not advance it.
what_it_does: If adopted, the bill would have provided continuing FY2019 funding for several federal agencies through February 8, 2019, to prevent a partial government shutdown. It would also have added money for border barrier construction, disaster relief, and Medicaid programs. The summary describes provisions dated after February 8, 2018, and its title does not match the subject matter, so the details may not reflect the version the Senate voted on.

who_it_affects.group: Federal employees and contractors whose agencies rely on continuing funding
who_it_affects.how: They would have kept operating without a funding lapse while the bill's continuing resolution was in effect.

who_it_affects.group: People who receive Medicaid home and community-based services
who_it_affects.how: Spousal impoverishment protections would have been temporarily extended for them.

who_it_affects.group: People affected by recent wildfires, hurricanes, typhoons, and earthquakes
who_it_affects.how: They could have received federal disaster relief and related assistance funded by the bill.
